edits.replace:
If the script is not at that path, search for it:
```bash
find . -name "validate-config-json.py" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"
```

**Validating a SEQUENCE of configs.** When several ops.json files will be executed one
after another, validating each on its own is not enough: an anchor that is unique against
the current file can be duplicated, rewritten or deleted by an earlier config in the same
run, and the executor sees that state while the validator did not. Name the predecessors,
in execution order:

```bash
python3 .claude/operations/scripts/validate-config-json.py \
  --after phase1.ops.json --after phase2.ops.json phase3.ops.json
```

This is not optional for parallel-authored plans — configs written independently against
the same file are exactly the case that escapes single-config validation.

operations.description: Record the validator sequence mode under Unreleased/Fixed.

edits.replace:
### Fixed

- **`validate-config-json.py --after`: validate a config against the state its
  predecessors leave.** Edits within one config were already simulated cumulatively, so a
  missing or ambiguous anchor was caught — but each config was measured against the file
  on disk, and a *sequence* was not. An anchor unique against HEAD can be duplicated or
  rewritten by an earlier config in the same run: four configs authored in parallel
  against one file each validated APPROVED and three then failed in the executor. `--after`
  projects the predecessors' edits in memory first, so the gate now agrees with the engine.
  The existence guards are projection-aware too, so a config may edit a file an earlier
  one creates.
